rows.notes: The cited work is a systematic literature review (24 peer-reviewed articles, 2001-2018) on factors influencing adoption of drip irrigation in India; it reports no data, experiment, survey or model runs of its own. Q1 is therefore 'no' and all other questions 'no'. Moreover, the review's own synthesis argues the opposite of the claimed direction: it states that mere adoption of micro-irrigation will not result in water conservation because farmers expand irrigated area, increase cropping intensity or shift to water-intensive crops (rebound effect), and that water savings on experimental plots do not translate to farm level. Fertiliser-saving (fertigation efficiency) is only mentioned as a finding of cited studies (Narayanamoorthy 2004b etc.), not as the review's own result.

notes: Full text appears complete. Study is a review, not a primary study; its conclusions caution against assuming water conservation from micro-irrigation adoption, so the citation misrepresents its thrust.
